title: The Capstone Bug: Slow, Then Dead
description:
**SITUATION:**

A production-shaped job on this cluster runs fine for several minutes, then slows dramatically, then one executor dies. Mentors will ask what you looked at. The Master UI, a worker log, and the executor's own memory breakdown each show a different piece of the story. No single source is enough.

This capstone combines Labs 1.2–1.6: read UIs as instruments, follow stages and tasks, ask where cached data actually lives, keep the executor memory map in your head, and watch for worker-level pressure. The failure is memory-leak-shaped — growth over a timeline, not a single bad snapshot.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Watch the job through healthy → slow → dead; capture when each phase starts.
2. Pull signals from the Master UI, at least one worker log, and the executor memory breakdown (and code / prior config if needed).
3. Synthesize them into one root cause — a memory-leak-shaped caching (or retention) bug — before applying a fix.
4. Apply the fix and show the job no longer dies the same way.
5. Capture the timeline, three signals, root cause, and fix in the Investigation tab.

**SPEC:**

- Diagnosis cites at least three independent signals that agree on the same root cause.
- The write-up reads a timeline (when healthy, when slow, when dead), not a single UI screenshot.
- The fix addresses that cause; simply raising executor count without explaining the leak is not enough.
- Investigation tab is complete — every field filled. Submit stays off until it is.

hints: If you only open the Master UI, you will miss the worker-local story.
Slow-then-dead often means cache or storage growth over time, not an instant OOM on the first stage.
Compare Storage and Executors tabs across the timeline, not just at failure.
Fill the Investigation tab; Submit stays off until every field is filled.
